== Biography ==
Wesley Guynn Glasgow was born about 1818 in Tennessee, United States.

== Research Notes ==
=== Current Maryland and Smith County review, 23 October 2026 ===

'''New possible father: unknown → James Glasgow-2492, 35%.''' Select James Glasgow-2492, the older Smith County householder, as Wesley Guynn Glasgow-2476’s possible working father. Their maintained accounts cite James in Smith County in 1820 and 1840 and the younger Wesley/Neely household there in 1850. James’s approximate 1776 birth makes him about 42 at Wesley’s estimated 1818 birth, a comfortable direct generation. The older James is a specific existing local household, not an invented parent. This is the leading bounded catalogue comparison for the disconnected Wesley family; its same-county chronology is more specific than an otherwise unplaced Tennessee or Scottish Glasgow.

35% is a subjective, low-confidence estimate for the complete father-profile hypothesis. No inspected record calls Wesley James’s son, places them in one household, transfers land between them, or names Wesley’s parents. The cited 1820/1840/1850 census images and age-band counts were not newly inspected; FamilySearch required a security challenge and the linked Ancestry record required membership. Wesley’s memorial has no parent links, dates or photograph beyond an approximate birth/death note; it is not independent parent proof. Wesley’s identification with the indexed Neely and James’s earlier North Carolina ancestry are separate propositions. An uncle or other collateral relationship, another local James, an unrepresented father, and William-2130 (broad Tennessee context without a held Smith County association) remain alternatives. No mother is selected and no relative is moved solely because of a name, naming custom or Y-DNA premise.

[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XHLT-ZFG James’s 1820 Smith County census citation] · [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XHT1-FBP James’s 1840 census citation] · [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:MCDC-2BM Wesley’s 1850 Neely Glassgow citation] · [https://www.findagrave.com/memorial/28676194 Wesley memorial, inspected and no parents supplied].


=== Original census and will review — 31 October 2026 ===

The original 1820 Smith County census, page 58, household 716, has James Glasgow with one male under 10, one male 10–15 and one male 26–44; females comprise one under 10 and one 16–25. The age-band reading follows the standard column order and is consistent with the county transcription; this manuscript leaf has no column headings. The original 1840 page 270 has a James household with males 5–9, 10–14 and 60–69, two females 15–19 and one female 40–49. Those older male bands fit the circa-1776 James account, but do not identify him uniquely. An unnamed 1820 boy could fit Wesley’s estimated 1818 birth; no 1840 male 20–29 appears in this household. Wesley could already have left home, so that absence does not exclude paternity. The 1820 page groups G surnames and is not evidence that adjacent lines were physical neighbours.<ref>Smith County, Tennessee, 1820 federal census, p.58, household716, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:33S7-9YB8-KZY original]; compared with the same-event county transcription at https://www.tngenweb.org/smith/census/1820/58.htm and NARA’s 1820 census column guide. Original 1840 census, p.270, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:33SQ-GYB9-9V4J James Glasgow household]. Inspected 31 October 2026.</ref>

The original 1850 Smith County household 1186, lines 2–9, contains the head indexed as Neely Glassgow, 32, farmer, Virginia 29, and the six indexed children Joicy A 9, John W 8, Elizabeth D 6, Andrew G 5, Holly J 3 and James W 11 months, all recorded as Tennessee-born. This is the existing Wesley-family source, not a newly discovered household. The original head’s handwriting is compatible with Wesley/Wesly; the index’s Neely reading and the later-life identification are kept distinct. No parent is named and no relationship column appears in this schedule.<ref>Smith County, Tennessee, 1850 federal census, household1186, lines2–9, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:S3HY-DCYQ-2HC original]; same event as FamilySearch MCDC-2BM, head indexed Neely Glassgow. Inspected 31 October 2026.</ref>

James Glasgow Senior’s original Davidson County will is now located in volume 7, printed pages 407–408, FamilySearch images 233–234. It expressly names a son James and appoints him an executor. The closing probate entry records that a son/executor James qualified in April 1820; the recording heading is June 1820. The will is dated November 1819; no exact day is adopted from this reading. This replaces the earlier original-uninspected status. It confirms the named-son role underlying James-2492’s existing 94% assessment, while identification of that son with the Smith County adult remains a separate inference. It does not name Wesley or prove James-2492 was Wesley’s father. The original contains other family and property clauses; this review publishes only the checked son/executor scope, without assigning untraced beneficiaries to modern profiles.<ref>Davidson County, Tennessee, Wills and Inventories vol.7, pp.407–408, James Glasgow Senior, will dated November1819, proved April1820 and recorded June1820; FamilySearch [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:2:77TV-194P?lang=en&i=232&groupId=1909088 image233] and [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:2:77TV-1945?lang=en&i=233&groupId=1909088 image234]. Original scan inspected onscreen 31 October 2026; download contract-disabled.</ref>

Wesley-2476’s selected father James-2492 remains Possible at 35%; James-2492’s own father James-634 remains Confident at 94%. The census age slots are compatible household evidence, not named kin or independent birth entries. No new parent, exact vital date, maternal attachment, profile merger or confidence gain follows. The cited indexes and their newly inspected originals describe the same underlying events and are not independent witnesses.

Smith County probate access was tested in the same signed-in session. The bound Wills 1828–1859 volume 6 and Wills 1803–1896 index routes were unavailable for online viewing. The accessible Wills 1841–1859 volume 3 consists of loose papers/folders, not a simple bound will book: only images 6, 450, 470, 485 and 500 were sampled, including 1848–1850 folder context. No James Glasgow packet was located in that small sample. This is not a full file or county-wide absence claim, and does not establish that he left no will. The profile-held mortality citation remains an unverified lead: its September/1850 wording must be checked against the original schedule’s reference period before assigning a calendar death year.
